title: Called by the Sabbath Bells Away
description: Called by the Sabbath Bells Away in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 69 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Sabbath Hymn”, where the book credits them to the Sun. School H. B.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Called by the Sab-bath bells a-way, Un-to thy ho-ly tem-ple, Lord, I'll go, with will-ing mind to pray, To praise thy name and hear thy word.

lines: Called by the Sabbath bells away,
I'll go, with willing mind to pray,
To praise thy name and hear thy word.
O sacred day of peace and joy,
Thy hours are ever dear to me;
Ne'er may a sinful thought destroy
The holy calm I find in thee.
Dear are thy peaceful hours to me,
For God has given them in his love,
To tell how calm, how blest shall be
The endless day of heaven above.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
